part.text:
Done. Here's what I changed and why.

## Root cause

`Context.redirect()` only ran `encodeURI()` when the location contained a non-Latin-1 character (`[^\x00-\xFF]`). For plain ASCII locations, raw `\r`/`\n` passed through unchanged into `Location`. In the runtime, `Headers.set('Location', '/a\r\nb')` throws `"is an invalid header value"` (and on looser runtimes could allow response splitting / header injection).

## Fix — `src/context.ts:771-783`

Compute the multibyte-encoded location first, then always percent-encode any remaining raw CR/LF:

```ts
const encodedLocation = !/[^\x00-\xFF]/.test(locationString)
  ? locationString
  : encodeURI(locationString)
this.header(
  'Location',
  encodedLocation.replace(/\r/g, '%0D').replace(/\n/g, '%0A')
)
```

Ordering matters:
- `encodeURI` already turns raw CR/LF into `%0D`/`%0A` in the multibyte branch, so the replace is a no-op there (no double-encoding to `%250D`).
- ASCII locations keep their existing behavior for valid URLs — pre-encoded `%XX`, `%3A%2F`, invalid `%hello`, etc. are untouched — while raw CR/LF get escaped.
- Already percent-encoded input (`%0D%0A`) is preserved, not re-encoded.

## Regression tests — `src/context.test.ts:118-141`

- Raw `\r\n` in an ASCII location → `%0D%0A` (302 preserved).
- Raw `\r` and `\n` individually → `%0D` / `%0A`.
- Already percent-encoded `%0D%0A` input → left as-is (no double-encoding).
- Multibyte + CR/LF → existing multibyte encoding plus `%0D%0A`, encoded exactly once.

## Verification

`pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts` → **67 passed (1 file)**, `context.ts` at 100% branch coverage. Changes are left unstaged for review.
